# SEO-354: Restore page state from the persisted event

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

Code that must run when a document is shown again inspects the persisted flag on the show event and takes the restoration path, rather than assuming the load handler will run.

## Rationale

On a restored document the load sequence does not repeat, so anything the page needed to do on becoming visible - refresh a timer, resume playback, re-read a value - never happens unless the restoration path exists.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "javascript_app",
    "has_router"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Add the show handler alongside the existing initialisation and branch on the persisted flag, keeping the two paths in one place so they cannot drift. Do not disable restoration in order to make the load path run again.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Trigger a restored navigation and confirm the state the page depends on is correct afterwards without a refetch.
- Evidence: `BROWSER`, `LOG`, `FILE`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: This record concerns correctness after restoration rather than any search behaviour, and it is included because the previous record makes restoration possible.
